title: Build a Writable Events API
summary: Extend the read-only Events API with validated POST, PATCH, and DELETE routes plus predictable client errors.

sketchBlocks.title: Turn the read API into a controlled writable service
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The campus events team can already list, filter, and inspect events. Staff now need controlled write operations.

Extend that same service without breaking the read contract. Add JSON body parsing, POST, PATCH, DELETE, validation, deliberate success statuses, and consistent client-facing errors.

Keep the existing GET collection, filter, resource, and missing-resource behavior working. Data remains local and in memory in this module.

sketchBlocks.title: Each write milestone extends the same complete service
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The ten milestones are cumulative.

**Step by step:** enable body parsing, add a pure validator, create resources, use the creation status, reject invalid creates, establish PATCH lookup, apply partial updates, add DELETE, handle missing mutation targets, and finally verify the whole writable contract through localhost.

Every later `starterCode` is the complete previous solution.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 1: Enable JSON request parsing
quizDraft.prompt: Start from the completed read API. Register Express JSON middleware before the routes so later write handlers can read `req.body`.
quizDraft.hint: Do not change the working GET routes; only add the shared parser before them.

help.concept: Write routes need parsed JSON bodies while existing read behavior remains intact.
help.hint_1: Register the built-in parser immediately after application creation.
help.hint_2: Keep the collection, filter, resource, and 404 GET behavior unchanged.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 2: Validate new event input
quizDraft.prompt: Keep the read API and JSON middleware. Add `validateNewEvent(input)` returning invalid field names for missing/non-string `title` or `category`.
quizDraft.hint: The helper should report problems only; do not mutate the event collection inside validation.

help.concept: A focused validator separates input decisions from mutation logic.
help.hint_1: Collect field names in a new local list.
help.hint_2: Return the list after checking both required fields.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 3: Create an event
quizDraft.prompt: Keep every read capability. Add `POST /api/events`, generate the next local numeric id, build the event from `req.body`, push it once, and return it.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone establishes the mutation path; later milestones tighten its status and validation behavior.

help.concept: POST adds one new event without changing the existing read routes.
help.hint_1: Generate an id from the local collection.
help.hint_2: Build one object, push it once, and respond with that same object.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 4: Return created status
quizDraft.prompt: Keep the POST route and change its successful creation response to status `201` while preserving the created JSON body and all GET behavior.
quizDraft.hint: Only the successful POST response status changes in this milestone.

help.concept: Creation has a more specific success outcome than a normal read.
help.hint_1: Keep the same created event in the body.
help.hint_2: Do not change the GET routes.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 5: Reject invalid creates
quizDraft.prompt: Call `validateNewEvent(req.body)` before generating an id or pushing. Invalid input returns status `400` JSON with `error: "Validation failed"` and `fields`; valid creates remain `201`.
quizDraft.hint: The invalid branch must return before id generation or mutation.

help.concept: Validation protects the in-memory collection from malformed create requests.
help.hint_1: Inspect the returned field list before creating the resource.
help.hint_2: Keep one predictable JSON shape for invalid create responses.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 6: Find an event for updates
quizDraft.prompt: Add `PATCH /api/events/:id`. Convert the id, find the matching event, and return the located representation for now. Keep POST and all GET routes working.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone establishes update lookup; field changes and missing-target handling come next.

help.concept: PATCH begins by locating the exact resource identified by the route parameter.
help.hint_1: Normalize the route id before comparison.
help.hint_2: Use the existing events collection for lookup.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 7: Patch supplied fields
quizDraft.prompt: Keep the PATCH lookup. Update only supplied `title` and `category` using explicit undefined checks, then return the updated event with status `200`.
quizDraft.hint: An omitted field must retain its existing value.

help.concept: PATCH performs a partial update of allowed fields.
help.hint_2: Return the same event after field updates.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 8: Delete an event
quizDraft.prompt: Add `DELETE /api/events/:id`. Find the matching array index, remove exactly one event with `splice`, and return status `204` with no body.
quizDraft.hint: Locate the target index before mutating the array.

help.concept: DELETE removes one identified resource and returns an intentional no-content success.
help.hint_1: Use the route id to locate one array position.
help.hint_2: Remove one item and send the no-content response.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 9: Handle missing mutation targets
quizDraft.prompt: Keep PATCH and DELETE behavior, but return status `404` JSON `{ error: "Event not found" }` when either mutation target is absent.
quizDraft.hint: Both mutation routes need a missing-target branch before state changes.

help.concept: Mutation routes must distinguish an existing target from a missing resource.
help.hint_1: PATCH branches on a missing event object.
help.hint_2: DELETE branches on the missing index sentinel.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 10: Verify the complete writable API
quizDraft.prompt: Keep the full API. In the local listen callback, verify valid create, invalid create, PATCH, DELETE, missing PATCH, and missing DELETE; log statuses and close the server.
quizDraft.hint: Use only localhost requests against the service you just built.

help.concept: Final verification exercises the write contract without public-network dependencies.
help.hint_1: Create one valid resource first so update/delete have a real id.
help.hint_2: Include successful and missing/invalid outcomes before closing.
